newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, solid gains predicted. [CORRECTED 15:51 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, solid gains predicted. [CORRECTED 15:51 GMT]

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Tuesday with significant gains in blue chips and traders predicted solid gains for leading issues.
"Main issues will definitely be rising," a trader at brokerage Metroholding told Reuters. "I also expect both (confectioner) Kras and Podravka to continue this (growth) trend."
* Of six active issues two rose, three were flat and one was down.
* Biggest gainer, drugs firm Pliva, was up 500 kuna to 12,000 on volume of 582 shares. Its GDRs, representing 1/50 of each share, traded at $47.87-$48.25 on the London Stock Exchange.
* Another blue chip, Zagrebacka banka, was up 35 kuna to 710 with 4,715 units (Corrects from 35 units) sold.
* Confectioner Kras closed flat at 275 kuna after peaking at 290 kuna on volume of 775 shares.
* Food processor Podravka was flat at 230 kuna with 365 shares trading.
* Hotelier Suncani Hvar was unchanged at 45 kuna and 484 units changed hands.
* Another hotelier Laguna lost 10 kuna to 800 but sold only ten shares.
* Volume down at 6,931, turnover up at 10.6 million.
